hypotheses in machine learning.

We go out and we
collect the data.

We try different models.

predictive tool or

Statistical approach

just looking for patterns in the

So supervised learning

trying to understand the
data and create clusters
from your data.

You're actually trying to
predict something, typically.

And what you do is you
divide your data into three

sets, training set,
a validation set,

and a test set because,
remember, what we're doing here
is not--
we haven't got a hypothesis.
We've just got a lot of data.

And so, typically, you
put about 60% of your data

into the training set, 20% into
the validation set, and 20%
into the test set.

And hopefully, you've
got quite a lot of data.

So you develop different
models using the training set.
So you try out different models.

And we'll see some examples
of this in a moment.

And you compare those
models using validation set.

Say, well, this model seems to
do better than this other model
when tested on--

the parameters of the
model are determined
using the training set.

And then you can see
how well the models work

on the validation
set and decide which

seems to be the best model
for explaining the data.

Typically, you can find a really
complex model, sometimes anyway,

that will explain the
data in the training set

but then it does not do
well on the validation set.
So the model can be too complex.
So we'll see.

So you want to,
typically, you want

to-- a rule of thumb is
you want to increase model

complexity until the model
starts to perform worse
on the validation set.

So once you've chosen
a particular model,

you can increase its complexity
and the parameters, and so on.

But as soon as it
starts to perform worse

on the validation
set, you know you've
overfitted the training set.

And then the test set
is kept to one side.

And it's not being involved
in the selection of the model

And so it provides a good
final out-of-sample indication

chosen model works.

Linear regression would

an artificial neural network is

to predict these variables in

about a neural network

is that you're going
through a number of stages

in predicting the
output from the input.

So we're not writing down
a nice, neat equation

for the relationship between
the output and the input

parameters of that equation.

We're saying there's
